deep.reconstruction:
The page is written sideways (rotated 90 degrees) and holds a single line: x/(1-x) = x + x^2 + x^3 + ... + x^16. This is the geometric series for x/(1-x), cut off after x^16.

Context from the neighbouring pages:
- Folio 102 recto computes (1-x)(1-x^2)(1-x^3)... times {1 + x/(1-x) + x^4/((1-x)(1-x^2)) + ...} as a power series up to x^36.
- It obtains 1 - x^2 - x^3 + x^9 + x^11 - x^21 - x^24 + ...
- It identifies this, via the Jacobi triple product with p = x^(5/2), q = x^(1/2), as the product of (1-x^(5n+2)), (1-x^(5n+3)) and (1-x^(5n+5)) over n >= 0.
- Dividing out gives the first Rogers–Ramanujan identity: 1 + sum_{n>=1} x^(n^2)/((1-x)...(1-x^n)) = 1/prod_{n>=0} (1-x^(5n+1))(1-x^(5n+4)).

This verso is almost certainly scratch work for that numerical check. It expands the second term x/(1-x) of the Rogers–Ramanujan series as a truncated power series, so it can be added to the expansions of x^4/((1-x)(1-x^2)), x^9/..., and so on, and then multiplied by the truncated Euler product. The specific purpose of the cut-off at x^16 is not stated on the page; in my reading it is just a working truncation for the term-by-term expansion. There is no derivation beyond the series identity itself.
